name: Brigade Hotel Ventures Ltd
title: Brigade Hotel Ventures Ltd - 544457 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Hotel operator with no capacity-cycle signal: Q4 RevPAR +6% on ADR +7% and flat 78% occupancy, but revenue only +8% and F&B hit by war cancellations of INR7-8 crore; FY27 capex ~INR3,600 crore is a growth plan, not discipline.

triggers.label: Cancellations ₹7-8 crore Apr-Jun
triggers.quote: we also got some cancellations worth about INR7 crores to INR8 crores, but we are trying to make that up with more domestic business

summary.headline: Brigade Hotel Ventures Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 13% to INR58 crores at a 39.7% margin, with PAT up to INR25 crores from INR13 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total income grew 8% YoY to INR146 crores, led by a 7% rise in ARR to INR8,066 with occupancy steady at 78%, giving RevPAR of INR6,295 (up 6%). PAT nearly doubled to INR25 crores, helped by lower finance costs after debt repayment and higher interest income on fixed deposits. F&B revenue fell about 3% YoY on INR7-8 crores of war-related cancellations, and GST 2.0 cost 1.4 points of EBITDA margin in the quarter. Management said April-June also saw INR7-8 crores of cancellations, offset partly by domestic demand; the call also laid out a INR3,600 crore capex plan and an ARR path toward INR14,000 by FY31.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR13 crores in Q4 FY25
+15% YoY vs INR167 crores; about 19% excluding ~INR6 crore additional property tax

segments.name: Rooms
segments.commentary: Room revenue rose about 7% YoY in Q4 on ADR growth of about 7% with occupancy held; Bangalore ADR growth slowed as the Aero show comparison and March cancellations forced lower-paying group fill-ins.

segments.name: F&B
segments.commentary: F&B revenue declined about 3% YoY in Q4 after INR7-8 crores of cancellations, about 5% of the quarter's business; full-year revenue growth was 12%.

segments.name: Bangalore hotels
segments.commentary: FY26 ADR grew 13% and RevPAR 12%; Q4 ADR growth was lower than other markets, with Q4 RevPAR up about 5%.

guidance_outlook: Kochi hotel to move from Four Points by Sheraton to Courtyard by Marriott in the coming quarter; management expects a mid-teens to double-digit ADR uplift.
Courtyard by Marriott Chennai World Trade Center (45 keys) targeted for Q3 FY27 opening.
Planned capex of about INR3,600 crores, of which INR400 crores was invested by FY26; about 60% to be debt-funded, remainder from internal accruals.
Internal accruals expected to exceed INR1,000 crores in coming years.
ARR projected above INR10,000 by FY29 and above INR14,000 by FY31, versus about INR7,500 today.
Management sees a gap to lift portfolio occupancy from 78% to mid-to-low 80s and says operating margins could reach about 37.5-38% without one-offs and GST impact.
Plans to add two or three restaurants at Gift City, which has a liquor licence and limited competition for three to four years.
capex_capacity: Planned capex of about INR3,600 crores; INR400 crores invested through FY26; about 60% debt-funded.
Courtyard by Marriott Chennai WTC (45 keys) targeted for Q3 FY27, in the OMR business district.
Kochi brand conversion from Four Points by Sheraton to Courtyard by Marriott underway, expected in the coming quarter.
Gift City: plans capex for two more restaurants alongside the existing F&B outlet.
Renewable energy share at 61%, with some hotels above 90%.
Management is looking for acquisition targets this year, but has not yet narrowed one down.
demand_pricing: Domestic business is about 73% of mix and international about 27%, versus the pre-war mix; management said the domestic/foreign split used to be about 70:30 and expects a return to about 30% foreign FTA over time.
Channel mix: transient 50%, negotiated contracts 25%, group 15%, miscellaneous/crew 10%. OTAs make up about 60% of retail, roughly 30% of total occupancy.
About 30% of room nights sell below INR7,500, the GST 2.0 threshold; management is working on inclusions and room categorisation to lift these above INR7,500.
Three of nine hotels are above INR7,500 ARR on an annual basis; one more is borderline.
MICE and large events dependent on foreign travellers were cancelled; management hopes some will return later in the year but cannot say which.

qa_highlights.question: Why was other income high in the quarter, and was there a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher interest on fixed deposits drove the increase, plus a INR4.7 crore reversal of creditors no longer payable.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the war hurt F&B, and what is the April outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: F&B revenue fell about 3% QoQ with INR7-8 crores of Q4 cancellations; similar cancellations continued in April-June, partly offset by domestic business. ADR rose 7% and occupancy held at about 78%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating margin range going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin would have been about 37.5-38% without the input tax credit loss, the one-off property tax and GST effects; margins should rise as ARR increases.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth (about 2%) lag RevPAR growth (about 6%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Room revenue rose about 7% but F&B fell about 3%, so total operating revenue grew about 2%; full-year revenue grew 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Bangalore's RevPAR divergence occur in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Bangalore Q4 ADR grew less because of the prior-year Aero show comparison and March cancellations, requiring lower-paying groups; April trends have improved.

qa_highlights.question: How will GST 2.0 be addressed and what is the Gift City position?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% of room nights are below INR7,500; management is using revenue strategies and expects 3-4 years before new Gift City supply. Two or three more restaurants are planned there.

risks_watch: Cancellations of about INR7-8 crores per month since March, and the timing of MICE and event recovery.
Gas supply: 4 hotels run on PNG and the rest on LPG; management reports no hotel ran out of gas but is shifting to induction.
GST 2.0 input tax credit reversal: about 30% of room nights are below INR7,500 ARR, a 1.4-point Q4 margin hit and a 0.8-point FY26 hit.
Foreign FTA mix down to about 27% from about 30%, depending on how the war-related travel pullback unwinds.
Acquisition pricing: management says buying assets is costlier per key than building.
Execution on Kochi conversion and Chennai opening in Q3 FY27; the capex is about 60% debt-funded.
Bangalore ADR softness in Q4 may persist if lower-paying groups keep filling rooms.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic demand, pricing and the growth pipeline, but cautious about international and MICE demand because of the war-related cancellations. Management was more hedged on margin recovery and on when cancelled events will return, and said it could not predict which would come back.
key_quotes: So the good thing is at least the domestic demand is remaining robust, so we are doing our best to make up for the loss in revenue through more domestic business.
So at this point in time, we're definitely open to acquiring assets, but when you're a builder, acquiring comes at a much more expensive cost per key.

So occupancy we don't want to compromise and we are working on our revenue strategies by coming up with more categorizations of rooms and inclusions and other things so that we get to that INR7,500 plus marks for these other hotels as well.

adds.what: Courtyard by Marriott Chennai World Trade Center, 45 keys
Kochi hotel brand conversion from Four Points by Sheraton to Courtyard by Marriott (existing keys, ADR uplift expected)
Two or three additional restaurants at Gift City

growth.why: Management guides ARR above INR10,000 by FY29 and INR14,000 by FY31 from about INR7,500 today, backed by a INR3,600 crore capex plan (INR400 crore spent), the 45-key Chennai hotel targeted for Q3 FY27 and the Kochi brand conversion with a mid-teens to double-digit ADR uplift; no revenue growth % is given, and the INR7-8 crore April-June cancellations are offset only partly by domestic demand.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: next 2-4 quarters, as GST 2.0 and one-offs fade
rows.why: Q4 EBITDA margin was 39.7% with GST 2.0 costing 1.4 points; management says margins could reach about 37.5-38% ex one-offs and GST effects, and ARR rising toward INR10,000 by FY29 should lift it further.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY28 (Kochi conversion, coming quarter); Q3 FY27 (Chennai
rows.why: Chennai Courtyard (45 keys) targeted for Q3 FY27 and Kochi brand conversion underway for the coming quarter, but these are existing or small key additions (45 keys against a portfolio of nine hotels) and capex of INR400 crores of INR3,600 crores is spent so far.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupancy held at 78% (FY26 76.1%) and the April-June INR7-8 crore cancellations are only partly offset by domestic demand, so volume growth depends on MICE and foreign travellers returning, which management cannot time.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: already announced; disbursement over coming years
rows.why: A INR3,600 crore capex plan is already stated (INR400 crores invested by FY26, about 60% debt-funded) and occupancy at 78% with the stated gap to mid-to-low 80s supports further deployment; management is also scouting acquisitions with no target yet narrowed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 EBITDA grew 15% (about 19% ex ~INR6 crore property tax) and RevPAR rose 10%, but April-June cancellations of INR7-8 crores and the Bangalore ADR slowdown cap upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: INR7-8 crores of cancellations per month since March and FTA mix down to about 27% from about 30% could drag F&B and room revenue, and GST 2.0 still hits margins (1.4 points in Q4).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Q1 FY28 (Kochi) and Q3 FY27 (Chennai); Gift City restaurants
rows.why: Kochi moves to Courtyard by Marriott with mid-teens to double-digit ADR uplift expected in the coming quarter, Chennai 45-key Courtyard targeted Q3 FY27, and two or three Gift City restaurants planned.

rows.label: Net cash of INR110 crores at 31 Mar 2026 vs ~60% debt-funded capex plan
rows.why: Net cash of INR110 crores and internal accruals expected above INR1,000 crores in coming years, but the 60% debt-funded share of the INR3,600 crore plan will add borrowings as capex is deployed.

rows.label: Rooms below INR7,500 ARR (GST 2.0 threshold)
rows.why: About 30% of room nights sell below INR7,500 and only three of nine hotels are above that ARR; management is working on inclusions and room categorisation, which could lift ARR but is not yet quantified.

rows.label: MICE and foreign-travel event recovery
rows.why: MICE and large events dependent on foreign travellers were cancelled and management hopes some return later in the year, but cannot say which, while FTA mix is about 27% vs about 30% before.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic demand, pricing, ARR path to INR14,000 by FY31 and the Chennai/Kochi pipeline, but cautious on international and MICE recovery and hedged on margin recovery and cancellation timing; analysts probed other income, F&B weakness, revenue lagging RevPAR and Bangalore
